definitions.explanation: A school for children aged 6-12, covering grades 1-6 in Japan.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}は{来年|らいねん}{小学校|しょうがっこう}に{入|はい}ります。
examples.english: My child will enter elementary school next year.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}は{家|いえ}から{近|ちか}いです。
examples.english: The elementary school is close to my house.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}の{先生|せんせい}になりたいです。
examples.english: I want to become an elementary school teacher.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}の{時|とき}は{毎日|まいにち}{歩|ある}いて{通|かよ}いました。
examples.english: When I was in elementary school, I walked there every day.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{小学校|しょうがっこう}では{給食|きゅうしょく}が{出|で}ます。
examples.english: School lunches are served at elementary schools in Japan.

notes:
{小学校|しょうがっこう} is elementary school, the first stage of Japan's compulsory education system.

STRUCTURE:
- Ages: 6-12 years old
- Grades: 1-6 ({一|いち}{年生|ねんせい}〜{六|ろく}{年生|ねんせい})
- Duration: 6 years
- Part of {義務|ぎむ}{教育|きょういく} (compulsory education)

JAPANESE SCHOOL SYSTEM:
- {小学校|しょうがっこう}: elementary school (6 years)
- {中学校|ちゅうがっこう}: middle school (3 years)
- {高校|こうこう}/{高等学校|こうとうがっこう}: high school (3 years)

RELATED VOCABULARY:
- {小学生|しょうがくせい}: elementary school student
- {入学|にゅうがく}する: to enter school
- {卒業|そつぎょう}する: to graduate
- {給食|きゅうしょく}: school lunch

NOTE:
Public elementary education is free. Most students walk to their local school and wear a backpack called {ランドセル}.
